info.title: IBM watsonx Orchestrate API
info.description:
The watsonx Orchestrate Server provides a set of APIs to power the watsonx Orchestrate AI assistant. It includes the following core services:

* AI Agent - a built-in AI assistant that powers the Orchestrate end-user experience.
* Assistant Runs - use the operations of this method to run a specific assistant, or get the details of runs for an assistant.
* AI Assistant - a service layer for interacting with the assistants that are added to the chat.
* Message Threads - a chat history and async message tracking store.
* Default Agent Settings - a method to get or update the current settings of the AI agent for the tenant that is associated with the authenticated user.

confirm_routing.title: Confirm Routing
confirm_routing.description:
Defines whether users must receive a confirmation message before they route to another AI assistant during a conversation in the chat. 

 The routing confidence of the AI agent supersedes the configuration of `confirm_routing`. The AI agent route to AI assistants based on the confidence that the AI agent has that a specific AI assistant is the best match for routing. The routing confidence is determined by the [conversation context](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/watsonx/watson-orchestrate/current?topic=using-ai-chat#routing). 
 When the routing confidence is high, users don't receive the confirmation message even if the value of `confirm_routing` is set to `true`. 

 For the `confirm_routing` property, you can define the values as described: 
 - `true`: Enable the request for users to confirm if they want to switch between AI assistants in the chat. 
 - `false`: Disable the request for users to confirm if they want to switch between AI assistants in the chat. 

 The value of `confirm_routing` is `true` by default.

 - The content cannot surpass the maximum limit of 50 characters.

 - The content must have at least 2 characters that are alphabetic. 

 Alphabetic characters are those characters defined in the Unicode character database as 'Letter'.

description.description:

 The content must comply with the following requirements: 

 - The content cannot be empty. 
 - The content cannot surpass the maximum limit of 500 characters. 
 - The first character of the content must be alphabetic. 
 - The content must have at least 2 characters that are alphabetic. 

 Alphabetic characters are those characters defined in the Unicode character database as 'Letter'.

 - `true`: The content of the welcome message or description uses the default content and not a customized content. 
 - `false`: The content of the welcome message or description uses a custom content.

HTTPBearer.description:
The authorization token used for the request. The supported token type depends on the deployment that your instance is on: 

 - For watsonx Orchestrate on AWS, use the JSON Web Token (JWT) to authorize your request. For more information about how to generate an JWT by using an API key, see [Generating an API key](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/watsonx/watson-orchestrate/current?topic=api-generating-key) and [Generating the JSON Web Token](https://developer.ibm.com/apis/catalog/watsonorchestrate--custom-assistants/api/API--watsonorchestrate--generating-a-json-web-token#generatingjwt). 
 - For watsonx Orchestrate on IBM Cloud, use the IAM Access Token to authorize your request. For more information about how to generate an IAM Access Token by using an IAM API key, see [Generating an IAM Access Token by using an API key](https://developer.ibm.com/apis/catalog/watsonorchestrate--custom-assistants/Authenticating+to+the+API#ibm-cloud-offering). 

 Use the "`--header 'Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_BEARER_TOKEN'`" format for the header, where "`REPLACE_BEARER_TOKEN`" is the token that you generated.
